title: DarkDistill: Difficulty-Aligned Federated Early-Exit Network Training on Heterogeneous Devices

problem.claim: Federated aggregation of heterogeneous local early-exit networks creates cross-model exit unalignment, undermining difficulty-specific specialization.

gap.claim: Existing difficulty-aware training schemes assume centralized environments with sufficient data and do not fit real-world edge devices.

contributions.claim: DarkDistill is a federated Difficulty-Aligned Reverse Knowledge Distillation scheme for aggregating heterogeneous local early-exit networks.
The approach trains difficulty-conditional data generators and selectively transfers generated knowledge of specific difficulties among matched exits.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a novel Difficulty-Aligned Reverse Knowledge Distillation scheme named DarkDistill.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations report that DarkDistill outperforms the state of the art in both full-parameter and parameter-efficient fine-tuning of early-exit networks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Early-exit networks accelerate edge inference by adapting computational depth to input difficulty, and their effectiveness depends on difficulty-aware training.
Existing difficulty-aware training assumes centralized environments with sufficient data, which is incompatible with real-world edge devices.
Federated training of early-exit networks on heterogeneous devices introduces cross-model exit unalignment during global aggregation.
DarkDistill addresses the alignment problem through difficulty-conditional generators and selective knowledge transfer between matched exits.
The authors report improved performance over state-of-the-art methods across full-parameter and parameter-efficient fine-tuning settings.
